title: Command Pallet Multiple Displays
summary: The Command Palette monitor-order complaint appears covered by newer multi-monitor and topology-stability work in current CmdPal code.
next_action: Draft a comment pointing the reporter to the newer Command Palette monitor-topology fixes and ask for a retest on a current build if the problem remains.

confidence.rationale: The issue was filed on an older build, while current CmdPal code now uses stable monitor IDs, friendly display names, and explicit topology-change handling.

judgment.rationale: Current merged Command Palette monitor-topology work appears to cover the reported “laptop becomes display 3” symptom on dock/undock.
evidence: The issue is on PowerToys 0.100.2 and describes the laptop changing to display 3 after connecting additional monitors.
CmdPal Dock multi-monitor support landed in PR #46915 and introduced monitor-specific identities.
PR #49814 explicitly fixes dock/undock and monitor-topology instability by using stable monitor IDs and friendlier display identity handling.
judgment.recommended_action: Point the reporter to the newer CmdPal monitor-topology fixes and ask for a retest on a current build before opening new design work.

fix_assessment.rationale: Current merged Command Palette monitor-topology work appears to cover the unstable numbering/selection path reported here.

issue_context.summary: The reporter wants Command Palette to stay associated with the laptop’s primary display after docking, but the older build they used surfaced different display numbering than Windows.
known_information: The report is against PowerToys 0.100.2 from Microsoft Store.
The laptop display is primary in Windows Display Settings, but Command Palette settings showed it as display 3 after docking.
A screenshot and bug-report ZIP were attached.
inferences: This is likely a monitor-identity/topology-stability bug rather than a simple UI text mismatch, because the wrong display identity also affects where Command Palette moves.
The current CmdPal monitor-service and topology-reconciliation work looks intended to solve this class of dock/undock confusion.
issue_context.analysis: The issue predates the latest multi-monitor/topology hardening in CmdPal. Existing merged work is a better first answer than starting a second independent design track.
initial_investigation: Current MonitorService in src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Services/MonitorService.cs builds friendly display names and stable device IDs instead of relying on raw ordinal labels alone.
PR #49814 specifically mentions dock/undock and Win+P topology changes causing empty/misconfigured dock state, then fixes stable-ID recovery and debounce behavior.
No linked PR or active assignee was found on this issue itself.

actions.label: Point to Command Palette monitor-topology fixes

comment.body: This looks likely covered by the newer Command Palette multi-monitor and topology-stability work in PR #46915 and PR #49814. Those changes move CmdPal toward stable monitor identities and friendlier display naming, specifically for dock/undock and changing monitor topologies. Because this report was filed on 0.100.2, I would first ask for a retest on a current build before opening a separate design track; if the laptop still remaps to the wrong display, a fresh screenshot on the newer build would be the next discriminator.
